neet_phy_u12_t05_2.working: In series nR = 100 and in parallel R/n = 4. Multiplying gives R² = 400, so R = 20 Ω and n = 5.

neet_phy_u12_t05_3.working: 3 Ω and 6 Ω in parallel give 2 Ω, so the total is 6 Ω and I = 18/6 = 3 A. The voltage across the parallel pair is 3 × 2 = 6 V, so the current through 6 Ω is 6/6 = 1 A.

neet_phy_u12_t05_4.working: A: series gives 18 Ω. B: parallel gives 2 Ω. C: 3 + 6 = 9 Ω. D: 12 Ω parallel with 6 Ω gives 4 Ω. So A-IV, B-I, C-III, D-II.

neet_phy_u12_t05_5.working: A is true. B is true. C is false: in parallel, current divides inversely with resistance. D is true: equal potentials mean no current. E is false: R_series ≥ n² R_parallel, with equality for equal resistors, so it is never less. Correct set is A, B, D.
